inputs.root_cause: Continuing the corpus-completion pattern from FF6-EVENT-000290 (3 of 9 real ora diagnostic codes covered), built fixtures for the remaining 4 (ORA_THUMBNAIL_UNREADABLE, ORA_THUMBNAIL_NON_CONFORMING, ORA_MERGED_IMAGE_UNREADABLE, ORA_MERGED_IMAGE_NON_CONFORMING). The first fixture attempt crashed validate() with an uncaught OraValidationError instead of returning a report -- exposing that _baseline_asset_diagnostics' two `except OraError` clauses (thumbnail and merged-image branches) never caught OraValidationError, which read_png_metadata actually raises for a structurally-invalid PNG. Further investigation found the same class of bug in validate()'s own outer handler, which also missed OraLimitError -- meaning a malformed stack.xml (a common real-world case, not an edge case) or a resource-limit violation also crashed validate() instead of reporting.
inputs.obligation_targeted: No obligation status change -- this is a real production bug fix (exception-hierarchy mismatch) plus corpus/test completion for already-implemented validation code (ORA-BASELINEASSET-001/ORA-STACK-001), not a missing->implemented promotion.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 4 new committed .ora fixtures (each independently verified via a standalone repro to trigger its intended diagnostic before any test was written), 6 new tests including 2 explicit regression guards naming the bug (test_thumbnail_unreadable_is_reported_not_a_crash, test_mergedimage_unreadable_is_reported_not_a_crash) and a third for the broader malformed-stack.xml case (test_malformed_stack_xml_is_reported_not_a_crash).
inputs.regression_tier: full ora package suite plus 6-format regression, mypy --strict, ruff

execution_steps: 1. Checked format_factory.ora.codec.png_metadata's satisfies_thumbnail_constraints()/satisfies_merged_image_constraints() to determine exact constraint values (THUMBNAIL_MAX_EDGE=256, THUMBNAIL_BIT_DEPTH=8, MERGED_IMAGE_BIT_DEPTHS={8,16}).

2. Built 4 fixtures by mutating exactly one ZIP member of valid/minimal.ora each: thumbnail replaced with non-PNG bytes; thumbnail replaced with a valid-but-300x300 PNG; mergedimage replaced with non-PNG bytes; mergedimage replaced with a valid-but-4-bit-depth PNG (reusing the existing png()-builder pattern from test_obligation_lifecycle_and_write.py, hand-rolled via struct/zlib for IHDR/IDAT/IEND chunks).

3. First verification call (validate() on thumbnail-unreadable.ora) crashed with an uncaught OraValidationError instead of returning a diagnostic-bearing report. Traced to errors.py: OraError(FormatParseError) and OraValidationError(FormatValidationError) are SIBLINGS under format_factory.core.FormatFactoryError, not a hierarchy -- `except OraError` in _baseline_asset_diagnostics' two try/except blocks (thumbnail at line ~227, merged-image at ~262) does not catch the OraValidationError read_png_metadata actually raises for a bad PNG signature or malformed IHDR.

4. Checked validate()'s own outer handler (line ~342) for the same class of bug: parse_stack() (stack_xml.py) raises OraValidationError extensively (malformed XML, invalid numeric attributes, missing xres/yres pairs, etc.) and OraLimitError for resource violations -- neither caught by the outer `except OraError`. Confirmed with a direct repro: validate() on a document with malformed stack.xml crashed uncaught before the fix.

5. Fixed all 3 sites: imported OraLimitError alongside the already-imported OraError/OraValidationError; changed the two _baseline_asset_diagnostics except clauses to `except (OraError, OraValidationError)`; changed validate()'s outer except clause to `except (OraError, OraValidationError, OraLimitError)`, with a docstring note explaining the sibling-not-hierarchy relationship so the mistake isn't repeated.

6. Re-verified all 4 new fixtures plus the malformed-stack.xml repro now return proper diagnostic reports instead of crashing. Added 6 tests to tests/python/ora/test_obligation_invalid_corpus_diagnostics.py: one per new fixture (STRICT-mode-raises + validate()-reports pairs for the 2 'unreadable' cases, single-report tests for the 2 'non-conforming' cases), plus a dedicated malformed-stack.xml regression test.
7. Updated samples/by-format/ora/_provenance.yaml with all 4 new fixtures, explicitly noting the bug each one surfaced.

8. Ran mypy --strict (1 pre-existing, unrelated error at lifecycle.py:92 confirmed via git stash to predate this change -- not introduced by this slice), ruff (clean), the full ora suite (330 -> 336 passed, wait: actually 16 tests in the file vs 10 before = +6, matching the file's own test count), and the 6-format regression (3648 -> 3654 passed, +6, 0 failed).
